newsitem.title: CHILE: Small group of Escondida workers vote to strike.
newsitem.headline: Small group of Escondida workers vote to strike.

text.p: A small group of unionized workers at the huge Escondida copper mine in northern Chile, encompassing about 15 percent of the mine's work force, have rejected a company pay offer and voted to strike, said union leader Hugo Fernandez.
Although the votes have not yet been counted, the union was certain that the some 300 workers who have already voted, have supported the strike call, Fernandez told Reuters.
The rest of the mine's some 2,000 workers were not involved in the vote or any potential strike.
"From conversations we have had with workers, we believe the strike has been approved," he said.
"I am completely certain that all those who voted supported the strike."
The official results will be known at around 2200 local (0300 GMT Wednesday).
Union officials said the strike will start at 0800 local Friday (1300 GMT).
Escondida, the world's largest copper mine, is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp plc. It produced over 800,000 tonnes of copper in 1996.
